description:
Owner's law (2026-07-02): follow_up is an anti-northstar SMELL — a job imperatively enqueueing other jobs is control-flow smuggled into a dataflow engine. The northstar admits exactly two reasons work runs: a consumer WAITS on a named fact/product (pull), or a CHANGED REVISION wakes a recorded reader. Every push site leaks scheduling policy into producers (duplicate fires, late-enqueue re-runs, self-scheduling walkers). The .18.19 concluded-coalesce is a SCREEN on the push, not a cure — its removal criterion is zero emissions.

DOC ALIGNMENT CHECK (2026-07-02, northstar.html + pull-based.html read in full against current code): the "follow_up is forbidden" framing is pull-based.html's explicit Non-negotiable ("A consumer must not schedule an arbitrary producer to save itself"; "Follow-up producer poke: Forbidden ... Existing legacy code can remain only until the replacement is proven and deleted"). northstar.html itself is narrower and still TOLERATES follow_up specifically for legacy jobs ("Legacy jobs may enqueue follow-up jobs, but new artifact producers return product/fact waits instead") -- this migration arc is exactly the doc-anticipated process of retiring that legacy tolerance, not an invented stricter rule. Be precise in future notes: it's pull-based.html's non-negotiable being enforced, with northstar.html's text due for an update once this arc completes (the doc itself says as much).

CORRECTION to the .18.24 first-family KEEP-list (superseding the 2026-07-02T13:09 comment): that comment classified root.rs:77/:112 AnalyzeActivation follow_ups as KEEP ("genuine first-run demand for a just-minted activation"). This is NOT supported by the docs and may be WRONG. pull-based.html's Current State Audit explicitly classifies the structurally-identical `SeedActivation(A)` push as "Push"/bad, with reuse only "behind a demanded activation product" -- i.e. converted to pull, not kept as an imperative push. Verified empirically (2026-07-02): `Job::AnalyzeActivation` is ALREADY demand-driven via `demand_if_needed` on the product path (compiler.rs:353/362, jobs/backend.rs:166/176) -- there is a WORKING pull-driven producer-expansion path for this exact job kind. Yet jobs/root.rs:81 (seed_root) and jobs/root.rs:108 (seed_activation itself) STILL push it via follow_up. This is a duplicate mechanism, not a sole path -- exactly the shape of the disease the first family proved-and-deleted for LowerFunction/PlanEntryDispatch. UNLIKE the first family, this is NOT yet proven always-coalesced: a just-minted activation may not yet have any waiter that would trigger the demand_if_needed path, so the push could be load-bearing for first-run discovery. THIS NEEDS ITS OWN INVESTIGATION AND PROOF (or disproof) as the arc's SECOND FAMILY -- do not assume either KEEP or DELETE without tracing whether some caller-side wait (e.g. a CallSiteSummary demand that already gates on ActivationAnalyzed) is always established by the time seed_activation/seed_root fire.

TELEMETRY GAP (2026-07-02): pull-based.html prescribes a session-level proof mechanism -- `fz.compiler2.pull.session.finished` with `follow_ups=0` and `root_scans=0` as the acceptance gate for a fully-converted path. The product path (pull.rs's ProductDriver) already emits a conceptually similar `["fz","compiler2","pull","session","finished"]` event, but with `executables`/`producer_pokes` fields, not `follow_ups`/`root_scans`, and it covers the PRODUCT/artifact path only -- the legacy semantic-layer `follow_up: Vec<Job>` mechanism this ticket targets has no aggregate session-level counter, only the per-step `coalesced: [...]` telemetry the .18.24-first-family audit used ad hoc (and which fz-go4.18.28.5's audit found NOISY/nondeterministic across identical reruns -- HashSet iteration order). Consider adding a real aggregate follow-up-emission counter (or extending the existing session-finished event) as THIS ARC's own DONE-verification mechanism, rather than continuing to rely on noisy per-fixture job-trace diffing family by family.

INVENTORY (verified 2026-07-02 by the .18.19 removable-code audit; production emissions): jobs/body.rs (~72 refs — DeriveTypeDef, ReifyGuardDispatch pushes from lowering), jobs/semantic.rs (~66), jobs/root.rs (seed_root pushes -- LowerFunction+PlanEntryDispatch DELETED at e561842ce, first family; AnalyzeActivation at :81/:108 now the SECOND family target per the correction above, not KEEP), jobs/dispatch.rs, jobs/keying.rs, jobs/contract.rs, jobs/types.rs, jobs/source.rs, source_publish.rs, quoted_expander.rs, world.rs. Product-side jobs (artifact/runtime_demand/transport/backend/native) emit ZERO follow_ups already -- this matches pull-based.html's "new artifact producers return product/fact waits instead" requirement being already met on that path.

THE MIGRATION SHAPE (proven in-tree): consumers express missing prerequisites as FACT WAITS; the driver's fact->producer map (demand_product_fact_producer, compiler.rs / jobs/backend.rs) demands the single producer for a missing FactKey -- this is pull-based.html's "pull driver expansion from demanded product key to its single producer" pattern, already the working shape for SeedActivation/AnalyzeActivation's demand_if_needed calls. Extend that map to the remaining semantic facts (TypeDefined, GuardDispatchReified, FunctionDefined, LoweredBody, EntryDispatch, ...); convert each emission site to a wait; SeedRoot shrinks to publishing root facts only. Work consumers-backward per family (DeriveTypeDef pushes first — most numerous, most mechanical), one commit per family, trace-proven per the minimal-job-trace gate (job counts drop or hold; products byte-identical) -- but per the telemetry-gap note above, prefer proving each family via the ALREADY-WORKING demand_if_needed pattern (does a demand path already exist for this job kind?) plus a targeted always-coalesced proof, not raw job-trace count diffing alone.

WATCH ITEMS to resolve during migration: (1) semantic.rs:1255-1258 demands DefineModule(protocol) while waiting on ProtocolDispatch — the one site where a follow_up historically forced a concluded job's re-run as a wait-unblocker (proven never load-bearing, but resolve the producer relationship properly); (2) the coalesced-telemetry channel conflates agenda-dedupe with standing-conclusion suppression (scheduler.rs:257 vs :228-232) — split the observability when this lands.

DONE = rg shows zero production follow_up emissions; JobEffects::follow_up field deleted; the .18.19 coalesce screen deleted (nothing left to screen); scheduler wake paths = changed-revision only; docs updated (fact-engine.md drops 'legacy jobs may enqueue follow-ups'; northstar.html's follow_up tolerance clause updated once this lands, per the doc's own forward note). Blocked by fz-go4.18.22 (LANDED — this is now unblocked).

Safe to delete as this arc's first family (own commit). (2) KEEP-classified: root.rs:77/:112 AnalyzeActivation (genuine first-run demand for a just-minted activation); ALL other emissions are absence-gated wait+demand pairs (semantic.rs:219/1257/1301/1492/1647/2265, dispatch, body, keying, source, world.rs:2094/2102, quoted_expander, source_publish) — these are the wait-implies-demand conversion targets. title: Migrate the semantic layer off follow_up: work runs only via waits (pull) or changed-revision wakes
